title: A photo diary of food and feelings
description: A photo, the time and a short note about hunger, fullness or mood. You can look back over your records without any obligatory calorie counting.

blocks.text: Some people need a food diary where they don’t have to look up products and count calories. One review author values precisely the absence of numbers and of judgments about food. It is a distinct way of recording experience, not a universal replacement for other diaries.

quote.text: Finally, a food tracking app that is extremely simple, intuitive, and non-triggering for those of us with a history of disordered eating. No calories, no green/yellow/red food categorization, no time wasted sorting through food databases.

blocks.text: Keep a photo of the meal and an optional note about the feelings or the circumstances. Let the records for a period be reviewed and let the person choose what to share with a professional. Don’t derive an automatic diagnosis or an assessment of the diet from a few photos.

Find out which records a person actually comes back to look at, and why. Simplicity is no proof that the format is safe in eating disorders; a promise like that should not follow from a single positive review.
